title: Service contract privacy adaptation and safe-fallback policy
author: Aditi Rao
content:
Overview

This decision record defines the privacy-adaptive service contract layer that mandates request payload sanitization, a graded response policy, and an automatic safe-fallback path for inference services. The goal is to reduce leakage of sensitive data (PII, credentials, secrets) from customer payloads while preserving low-latency inference and predictable unit cost. This doc specifies runtime requirements, API semantics, observability signals, rollout steps, and owner responsibilities.

Why we need this

- We operate multi-tenant hosted and private inference with a mix of customer-provided prompts and structured tool calls. Some payloads can contain high-risk fields (PII, PHI, secrets).
- Past incidents show accidental exposure through model output and telemetry; we need an explicit, centralized contract enforcement and fallback mechanism to prevent recurrence.
- Enforcement must be low-latency (<5ms median added per request for simple sanitization) and auditable.

Decision summary

We will adopt a Service Contract Privacy Adaptation Layer (SCPAL) implemented as:

1) A lightweight request preprocessor that performs classification and sanitization at three levels (none, redact, transform).
2) A policy engine that evaluates the contract hints and tenant config to select either: direct passthrough, sanitized passthrough, or safe-fallback to a gated, lower-fidelity model variant with deterministic output constraints.
3) Telemetry and trace enrichment that records sanitized fields (hashes only), sanitization decisions, and fallback invocations.
4) A throttled replay queue for requests that were transformed/fallbacked so product ops can review borderline decisions offline.

Runtime contract and API requirements

- New request header: X-RW-Contract-Hints (JSON string, max 512 bytes) — contains optional hints: expected_data_class, pii_risk, prefer_fallback. Clients may provide hints but the service must not trust them blindly.
- Response header: X-RW-Sanitization-Decision = [none|partial|redacted|transformed|fallback].
- Sanitization latency budget: 95th percentile <= 12ms, median <= 4ms for 99% of traffic under nominal load. Additive end-to-end SLO allowance: 10ms for contract enforcement on top of model latency budgets.
- Fallback SLO: fallback path should serve at least 95% of fallback requests within configured model tier latency SLA (default: 300ms p95 for interactive workloads).

Sanitization levels (config table)

| level     | description                                          | runtime effect                                    | telemetry recorded |
|-----------|------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|--------------------|
| none      | no modification                                       | passthrough                                       | decision = "none" |
| partial   | mask high-risk tokens, preserve non-sensitive context | in-place token masking (e.g., email -> ****@example) | masked_fields_count |
| redacted  | remove entire fields or spans                        | replaced with stable redaction token ([REDACTED]) | redacted_field_list (hashes) |
| transformed| deterministic canonicalization for structured data   | transform (e.g., 1111-2222 -> CARD_TOKEN_1)      | transform_map_hash  |
| fallback  | route to a safe, policy-gated model variant          | use lower-fidelity model with output filters     | fallback_reason_hash |
(We store only hashed identifiers of fields/keys; plaintext is never persisted in logs or metrics.)

Policy engine behavior

- Input signals: tenant config (tenant_id), contract hints, model capability manifest, prompt classification classifier score (0-100), and request cost estimate.
- Decision matrix (simplified):
  - If classifier_score >= 90 and pii_risk == high -> redacted or transformed depending on data shape.
  - If classifier_score between 60-90 -> partial.
  - If classifier_score < 60 but tenant has prefer_fallback=true -> fallback.
  - For structured tool calls with known schemas, apply schema-based transforms (see Prompt Data Classification playbook).

Observability and telemetry

Instrumentation must emit the following fields for every request (sample rates apply, see rollout):
- sanitization.decision (enum)
- sanitization.latency_ms (int)
- sanitization.masked_count (int)
- sanitization.redaction_hashes (list of short hashes, sampled)
- fallback.invoked (bool)
- fallback.duration_ms (int)
- request.pii_classifier_score (int)
- request.size_bytes (int)

Sampling and privacy: by default redact-sensitive telemetry and only emit hashes; default sample rate for full payload hash emission = 0.05 (5%). Increase sample rate only with legal/security approval.

Impact on other standards

- API standards: Add the new headers to the canonical request schema and update client SDKs. Clients must tolerate the X-RW-Sanitization-Decision header and treat transformed tokens as opaque.
- Coding standards: implement sanitization as a small, well-tested library with typed inputs/outputs and golden tests that assert no plaintext persists in logs or metrics. See tests guideline below.
- Infra standards: the SCPAL runs as a horizontally-scalable sidecar in hosted and dedicated offerings; in private deployments it can be enabled as an optional sidecar or inline library depending on customer preference. Sidecar must be able to run on CPU-only nodes and be resource-capped (default 0.25 CPU, 128MiB).
- Model-serving standards: fallback model variants must support deterministic output constraints and have a deterministic-output post-filter sidecar to remove hallucinated secrets.
- Observability standards: ensure traces include anonymized decision IDs and are correlated to model traces for end-to-end debugging without leaking PII.
- Performance standards: include sanitization in synthetic load tests and SLO budgets; regression gates will block model rollouts if sanitization increases p95 latency by >20%.

Testing and CI requirements

1) Unit tests for classifiers and transform logic with boundary cases (emails, SSNs, API keys, base64 blobs).
2) Golden redaction tests verifying that given sensitive payloads, sanitized outputs never contain original sensitive substrings.
3) Fuzz tests that generate edge-case structured payloads to ensure transformers do not crash or leak.
4) Integration test in the staging runtime with controlled sampling to validate telemetry masking logic.

Rollout plan

1) Stage 0 (2 weeks): feature flagged sidecar deployed to canary fleet (1% traffic). Sample telemetry at 100% locally, but persist no payloads; only hashes. Verify latency budgets.
2) Stage 1 (4 weeks): increase to 10% traffic; enable partial and redaction decisions; run manual evaluation of transformed outputs using replay queue.
3) Stage 2 (4 weeks): enable fallback policy for tenants with prefer_fallback=true; monitor fallback.invoked rates and model fidelity.
4) Stage 3 (8 weeks): global rollout for hosted API; private deployments opt-in. Create customer communication and migration notes.
5) Post-rollout (ongoing): quarterly review of classifier thresholds, add new rules for new PII patterns, and maintain a suppression list for false positives.

Operational runbook (high level)

- Alert: sanitization.rate_of_fallbacks > 0.5% for 10m -> Severity P2. Owner: eng-sre -> run query to determine tenant(s) and request samples via replay queue.
- Alert: sanitization.latency.p95 > 20ms for 10m -> Severity P1. Owner: eng-infra -> scale sidecar pool or investigate hot paths.
- Incident steps:
  1. Toggle feature flag to degrade to none or partial depending on impact.
  2. Open a secure investigation channel (restricted) and avoid sharing raw payloads.
  3. If leakage suspected, follow incident-response-security/ and contact the security on-call.

Ownership and contacts

- Product owner: Maya Chen (product -> model-platform).
- Engineering owner: Aditi Rao (serving-runtime team).
- SRE oncall: see eng-sre oncall roster.
- Security reviewer: Priya Patel.

Alternatives considered and reasons for rejection

- Client-side only sanitization: rejected because clients are inconsistent and may not run across private deployments; server-side provides uniform guarantees.
- Full payload logging with later redaction: rejected because risk of persistence of plaintext in backups and analytics systems.
- Blocking requests with PII: rejected as too disruptive for customers; prefer transform/fallback for continuity.

Consequences

- Positive: improved incident surface reduction for data leakage, consistent privacy guarantees across hosted/dedicated/private offerings, auditable decision traces.
- Negative: added complexity and cost; small added latency and operational overhead to tune classifier thresholds.

Open questions and next steps

- Determine legal-approved retention policy for replay queue (suggestion: 30 days, hashed-only unless explicit w/ customer consent).
- Define a tenant-level override workflow for enterprise customers requiring different default policies.
- Integrate a lightweight differential-privacy mode for analytics pipelines that rely on sanitized telemetry.

Appendix: example headers and CLI examples

- Example request header (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n     -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \n     -H "X-RW-Contract-Hints: {\"expected_data_class\":\"chat\",\"pii_risk\":\"high\"}" \n     -d '{"input":"Please summarize: My credit card is 4111-1111-1111-1111 and my SSN is 123-45-6789"}'

- Example response headers:
  X-RW-Sanitization-Decision: redacted
  X-RW-Sanitization-Version: 2026-01-01

- Example config snippet (tenant policy):
  tenant_policy: 
    prefer_fallback: false
    default_sanitization_level: partial
    allowed_transformers: [credit_card_canonicalizer, email_masker]
    telemetry_sample_rate: 0.05
